observation.visible_scene: Top-down close view of a small brass melting spoon with a pale-blue glass handle, resting on a black circular stand that has two dark wooden side handles. Inside the spoon bowl sit two star-shaped solids—a deep purple star on the left and a silvery-lavender star on the right—partly embedded in a milky pool streaked with pale green. The background (tan cardboard and a white printed cloth) is fixed. A faint orange glow is intermittently visible at the lower rim of the spoon bowl.
visible_changes: The purple star progressively loses its sharp five-point outline: its tips round off and by the later frames it has collapsed into a small irregular blob with a thin purple strand trailing to the left, while a purple smear spreads into the white pool around it.
The silvery star similarly softens and flattens, and the silvery area above/around it develops growing concentric swirl/foam-like textures that expand toward the upper-right rim.
The white-and-green liquid pool appears to spread and mix, with the green streaks becoming broader and the milky surface taking on more of the melted material as the two stars shrink in relief.
The orange glow at the spoon's base flickers on and off across frames but the spoon, handle, stand and background remain in fixed positions (no object translation and no evident camera movement).
outside_clip_unknowns: The state of the stars before t=0 and the final outcome after t=2.67s (e.g., whether they fully dissolve) are not shown.
The heat source producing the glow and the material identity of the stars/liquid are not visible within the segment.
uncertain_details: Whether the apparent spreading of the liquid is true volume increase or just redistribution as the solids deform cannot be confirmed from the frames alone.
Minor changes in highlight/reflection on the brass and on the stars could be lighting flicker rather than physical change.
